speaker: clown
line: [excited] Alright, quiet down! Duke Prospero's Royal Ball starts right now!

speaker: clown
line: [cheerful] Scan in at the gate, you're on Prince Hamlet's council tonight.

speaker: clown
line: [grand] This is Prince Hamlet. We mapped his entire brain, all hundred and sixty six thousand neurons of it.
note: 166,606 neurons: measured by brain/build_graph.py

speaker: clown
line: [playful] You're the Helmsman. Left and right, that's all you.

speaker: clown
line: [playful] You're the Liftmaster. Up and down are yours.

speaker: clown
line: [playful] You're the Wingmaster. Forward's your job, don't forget the brakes.

speaker: clown
line: [dramatic] You're the Seer. Only one who can see the Princess, and the Giant. So talk.

speaker: clown
line: [cheerful] We need four grapes for the banquet. Four of you, four grapes. Should be easy.

speaker: clown
line: [brisk] Wingmaster, ease forward. Let go to slow down. It's a grape, not a getaway.

speaker: clown
line: [brisk] Helmsman, left and right. Small taps, we're picking grapes, not storming a castle.

speaker: clown
line: [brisk] Liftmaster, up to grab it, down to drop it in. Try not to lose the crown.

speaker: clown
line: [encouraging] All together now. Slow down before the turn, that cup's taken enough hits today.

speaker: clown
line: [conspiratorial] Seer, Princess Miranda's near the cup somewhere. Find her and call it out.

speaker: miranda
line: [warm] Hello, Hamlet. Your Seer can find me. The rest of you would do well to listen to them.
note: Plays when the lesson starts, never by distance, so it can't hint where she is

speaker: clown
line: [delighted] All four delivered! Not bad, for a job that's mostly grape juice now.

speaker: miranda
line: [warm, amused] Four grapes, all in one piece. Father might even be impressed. Eventually.

speaker: clown
line: [upbeat] Tonight's the night. Duke Prospero announces Prince Hamlet and Princess Miranda's engagement. But first... one tiny errand.

speaker: hamlet
line: [pleased with himself] Four grapes, delivered, and not one spilled.

speaker: clown
line: [wry] Not even a taste. Remarkably disciplined.

speaker: hamlet
line: [proud, then alarmed] Perfectly steady... oh no.

speaker: clown
line: [dry] Innocent or not, the stain remains.

speaker: prospero
line: [indignant, raising his voice] Purple stains on your lips? Stumbling by the banquet cup, this morning of all mornings? Hamlet!

speaker: hamlet
line: [flustered] It was only a landing accident, Your Grace. A messy one, but an accident all the same.

speaker: prospero
line: [angry] Tonight of all nights I must trust you beside my daughter, and you cannot even arrive at breakfast steady on your feet?

speaker: hamlet
line: [desperate] I have not touched a drop, Your Grace! Ask my council, they were with me the whole time!

speaker: prospero
line: [cold, final] Then prove it some other way, for right now you show me nothing but the opposite. The announcement is suspended, until you do.

speaker: miranda
line: [gentle, pleading] Father, please, at least let him explain.
note: Nobody listens to her either; E01_P3 pays it off

speaker: prospero
line: [stern] Stay outside, until you can hold yourself together.

speaker: clown
line: [sighing] A royal misunderstanding. Naturally, no one listened to the ones who actually saw it happen.

speaker: hamlet
line: [determined] There, a window. Come, council, we may still set this right.

speaker: clown
line: [wry] Let us hope the window has better manners than the door.

speaker: tinman
line: [cold, contemptuous] Locked out of your own betrothal, Prince Hamlet? How very becoming of a future king.

speaker: tinman
line: [flat, mocking] My heart would go out to you, if I had one to spare. A family trait, I am told.
note: True gene fact: tinman flies grow no heart

speaker: tinman
line: [irritated, superior] This is my window, so we shall do this my way. Answer correctly, and you get pear nectar. Answer wrongly, and you may have more of whatever you have clearly already been drinking.

speaker: tinman
line: [crisp, testing] Here is your question, little prince. Does alcohol make one's balance and coordination... A, worse. Or B, sharper?
note: Tinman asks; the options stay on screen

speaker: hamlet
line: [nervous, murmuring] Council... a little help, please.

speaker: tinman
line: [dry] Take your time. I have nowhere better to be, apparently.

speaker: tinman
line: [matter-of-fact] The answer is A. Alcohol interferes with the exact brain functions used for balance and coordinated movement.
note: Plays after the answer, before the drink panel. Fact: NIAAA

speaker: tinman
line: [grudging, annoyed] Correct. How inconvenient. Pear nectar, as promised.

speaker: tinman
line: [delighted, mocking] Wrong. Utterly wrong. The grape cordial, then, as agreed.

speaker: clown
line: [mock-dramatic] And so the misunderstanding gains a sequel.

speaker: tinman
line: [dismissive, cold] Do try not to fall to pieces before you arrive, Prince Hamlet. Princess Miranda dislikes a scene. I would not know; I feel very little, one way or the other.

speaker: clown
line: [ominous] Below the window, storage. Below the storage, trouble.

speaker: clown
line: [cheerful] A fine inspection of the stonework. Now, let us try the opening.
note: After a spike hit; nondirectional

speaker: rutabaga
line: [flustered, irritated] Oh. You again. Or is it someone else? It hardly matters, you all look equally troublesome to me tonight.

speaker: rutabaga
line: [testy] Are you here for Princess Miranda? So is everyone, apparently, myself included, and I find it rather tiresome to keep explaining that.
note: He forgets whom he's courting (lore)

speaker: rutabaga
line: [muttering, annoyed] I wrote myself a question, so I would remember which drink goes to whom. Whom proved difficult to spell, but no matter. Answer it, and be quick about it.

speaker: hamlet
line: [urgent, polite] Count Rutabaga, we really do need the stairs.

speaker: rutabaga
line: [snippy] Yes, yes, the stairs. One question, and they are entirely yours, Prince Hamlet. Do stop hovering.

speaker: rutabaga
line: [reading slowly, irritated] Can heavy drinking interfere with forming new memories? A, no. B, yes. Whoever wrote this has dreadful handwriting. Oh. That would be me.
note: Rutabaga asks; the options stay on screen

speaker: rutabaga
line: [relieved, matter-of-fact] It is B. Alcohol can disrupt the forming of new memories. It does not erase the old ones, though. I have checked. More than once. For reasons I would rather not discuss.
note: Plays after the answer, before the drink panel. Fact: NIAAA

speaker: rutabaga
line: [surprised, pleased] Correct. New memories, yes, that was the important part. Pear nectar, then, for the one of us who remembered anything at all tonight.

speaker: rutabaga
line: [flustered, cross] Wrong! I had a rather cutting remark prepared for this moment, and now I cannot recall it. How fitting. The purple one, then, and good riddance.

speaker: rutabaga
line: [startled, alarmed] Oh! Now I remember why I came down here in the first place! Farewell!
note: The groan and thud upstairs play first

speaker: hamlet
line: [uneasy] What in the world was that?

speaker: clown
line: [wry] A sensible question. Naturally, we went up to answer it ourselves.

speaker: clown
line: [urgent] One minute before the inner gate closes. Quiet wings, council, quiet wings!

speaker: clown
line: [sighing] The gate won that round. Once more, and a little quieter this time.

speaker: cheapdate
line: [hiccup, irritated] Prince Hamlet. Of course it is you. I have two drinks, and apparently, only just enough patience.

speaker: cheapdate
line: [proud, slurring] Only half a grape's worth tonight. [hiccup] I consider myself a most efficient drinker. Unlike some engaged princes I could mention.
note: True gene fact: cheapdate flies get drunk on less alcohol

speaker: cheapdate
line: [sour, tipsy] Before you go swanning in there, a toast, and a test. Pass it, and take the pear. Fail, and you may share my purple vintage, and my evening.

speaker: cheapdate
line: [bitter, hiccup] A question about recovering afterward. A subject on which I have done extensive, and thoroughly regrettable, research. Unlike you, apparently.

speaker: cheapdate
line: [squinting, slurred] Does coffee undo alcohol's effect on one's judgment and coordination? A, yes. B, no. Choose carefully, Your Highness.
note: Cheapdate asks; the options stay on screen

speaker: cheapdate
line: [sheepish, hiccup] It is B. Coffee only makes one feel more awake. It undoes nothing at all. I have tested this claim thoroughly. And repeatedly. To my own detriment.
note: Plays after the answer, before the drink panel. Fact: NIAAA

speaker: cheapdate
line: [grudging, hiccup] Correct. Sharper than me tonight, which, I admit, is not saying very much. Pear nectar, for the prince who apparently thinks ahead.

speaker: cheapdate
line: [delighted, hiccup] Wrong! Purple for you, then, Prince Hamlet. Welcome to my level, for once.

speaker: clown
line: [shouting] Sir Cheapdate! Your chair is in the punch bowl again!
note: Clown is off-panel

speaker: cheapdate
line: [hiccup, mournful] My chair has arrived at the punch bowl before I have. Again.

speaker: hamlet
line: [relieved] At last...
note: Cut off by the crash

speaker: clown
line: [wry] The evening had other plans for that sentence.

speaker: clown
line: [dramatic] The Giant arrived. It brought neither invitation nor manners.

speaker: prospero
line: [alarmed] You? Hamlet, I told you to stay outside!

speaker: miranda
line: [surprised] Hamlet! Did you come in through the window?

speaker: hamlet
line: [pleading] The garden was not what it looked like, Your Grace. Please, let me explain.

speaker: prospero
line: [urgent, commanding] Then prove it. Keep that creature's attention. Outlast its swats until it abandons this hall.

speaker: hamlet
line: [resolute] Council, together now. We need not hurt it. We need only stay beyond its reach.

speaker: miranda
line: [worried] Then stay beyond its reach, Hamlet, and listen to your Seer.

speaker: clown
line: [excited] Ten dodges. One enormous temper. Let us see which one outlasts the other.
note: The objective text is on screen only, not voiced

speaker: miranda
line: [relieved] Oh, well flown, Hamlet!
note: Plays after the attack resolves, never at warning onset; the game picks one line from the pool

speaker: miranda
line: [excited] Yes! It missed you completely!

speaker: hamlet
line: [breathless, relieved] Missed me! Council, that was beautifully done.

speaker: clown
line: [delighted] Missed! The table takes another beating.

speaker: prospero
line: [grudging] Hm. Not entirely hopeless, I suppose.

speaker: tinman
line: [flat, unimpressed] Luck. Remarkably consistent luck, for someone so clumsy.

speaker: cheapdate
line: [hiccup, sour] Congratulations. Even a broken clock is right twice a night.

speaker: rutabaga
line: [confused, irritated] Which one is Prince Hamlet again? The one still flying? Fine. Good. Whatever that means.

speaker: miranda
line: [gasping] Hamlet! Are you hurt?
note: Plays after the attack resolves, never at warning onset; the game picks one line from the pool

speaker: miranda
line: [worried] Hamlet? Say something, anything at all!

speaker: hamlet
line: [dazed] Still here. Mostly crown.

speaker: clown
line: [wincing] Ooh. That one goes in the chronicle.

speaker: prospero
line: [scoffing] And this is precisely why I told you to stay outside.

speaker: tinman
line: [amused, cold] Splendid. Do that again, slower this time, so I may enjoy it properly.

speaker: cheapdate
line: [hiccup, wincing] Ooh, I felt that one. Sympathetically. And a little smugly.

speaker: miranda
line: [hopeful] Five, Hamlet! It is tiring!
note: Plays instead of an after-a-dodge line

speaker: clown
line: [encouraging] Halfway there. You can see it reconsidering its life choices.

speaker: miranda
line: [pleading] One more hit and Father steps in. Please, be careful!
note: Plays instead of an after-a-hit line

speaker: clown
line: [urgent] Careful, council. The next hit ends this. Trust your Seer.

speaker: miranda
line: [excited] One more, Hamlet! Just one more!
note: Plays instead of an after-a-dodge line

speaker: clown
line: [dramatic] Nine! One more, and this creature is finished.

speaker: clown
line: [triumphant] Ten swats survived. The Giant gave up, and went to squash something less troublesome.

speaker: prospero
line: [approving] You held your ground by never once holding still. Well flown, Prince Hamlet.

speaker: miranda
line: [soft, relieved] You are safe. Next time, find me before you volunteer yourself to a giant hand.

speaker: hamlet
line: [wry, tired] Next time, I shall simply bring flowers.

speaker: miranda
line: [laughing softly] Flowers would be lovely. Bring them, though. Do not become them.

speaker: prospero
line: [furious] First the garden. Now this. Stand back, Hamlet.

speaker: prospero
line: [breathless, furious] There. I have finished your task myself. My patience did not survive the effort.
note: Was Clown narration; Prospero now says it himself

speaker: miranda
line: [upset] Father, he endured three strikes trying to keep that creature away from us.

speaker: prospero
line: [cold] You expect my blessing after tonight? You shall not pass me, Prince Hamlet.

speaker: hamlet
line: [quiet, firm] Then let Miranda speak for herself, Your Grace.

speaker: clown
line: [wincing] His Grace decided to settle this personally.
note: The objective text is on screen only, not voiced

speaker: miranda
line: [scolding] Father! We do not throw things at our guests!
note: Plays after the attack resolves, never at warning onset; the game picks one line from the pool

speaker: miranda
line: [exasperated] Father! You are a duke, not a catapult!

speaker: prospero
line: [muttering, annoyed] Missed. How does something so small dodge so very much?

speaker: prospero
line: [breathless] I have... plenty more... where that came from.

speaker: hamlet
line: [breathless, pleading] Your Grace, I would much rather we simply talked this through!

speaker: clown
line: [wry] That floor has never been so thoroughly argued with.

speaker: miranda
line: [hopeful] One more, Hamlet! Father, you are quite out of breath.
note: Plays instead of an after-a-dodge line

speaker: prospero
line: [wheezing, defensive] I am... not... out of breath.
note: Prospero's reply to F_FOUR_MIRANDA; play them as a pair

speaker: miranda
line: [gasping] Father! How could you?
note: The one hit ends the fight; E02 follows

speaker: miranda
line: [gentle, firm] Father, thank him. Then, please, listen to him.

speaker: miranda
line: [soft but firm] Enough, Father. I love Hamlet. You do not get to throw things at the person I choose.

speaker: clown
line: [cheerful] For the record, he was delivering my grapes. The chalice splashed him. I was there to see it.

speaker: prospero
line: [soft, humbled] Then I judged you before I listened to you. Miranda, do you still wish this announcement to go ahead?

speaker: miranda
line: [soft] Yes. Because I choose it.

speaker: prospero
line: [warm] Then let the banquet begin again.

speaker: miranda
line: [warm, amused] And this time, Hamlet, do use the door.

speaker: clown
line: [delighted] A royal announcement, approved by Princess Miranda herself. The grapes, for once, abstained.

speaker: clown
line: [wry] Prince Hamlet's evening had reached the floor. The competition mistook this for an opening.

speaker: tinman
line: [smug, cold] Your Grace, I believe we can all agree there stands a far more composed candidate before you now.

speaker: cheapdate
line: [hiccup, eager] And one directly behind him! Slightly behind. Swaying, admittedly, but behind!

speaker: rutabaga
line: [confused] Which position am I applying for, exactly? Husband? It rather feels like husband.

speaker: miranda
line: [passionate] Enough. I never wanted a marriage chosen for me. Not by a contest. Not by any of you.
note: Her one passionate line

speaker: miranda
line: [calm, resolute] I can decide my own future.

speaker: clown
line: [soft] For once, the entire court had nothing useful to add. It was, in its own way, a peaceful ending.

speaker: clown
line: [brisk] Growing dizzier. Allow yourself more room to stop.
note: After a wrong answer raises dizziness; optional voice, the notice is on screen

speaker: clown
line: [alarmed] The Helmsman has fainted! Revive them, quickly!
note: Pre-generated form of H_FAINTED {role}

speaker: clown
line: [alarmed] The Liftmaster has fainted! Revive them, quickly!
note: Pre-generated form of H_FAINTED {role}

speaker: clown
line: [alarmed] The Wingmaster has fainted! Revive them, quickly!
note: Pre-generated form of H_FAINTED {role}

speaker: clown
line: [alarmed] The Seer has fainted! Revive them, quickly!
note: Pre-generated form of H_FAINTED {role}

speaker: clown
line: [gasping] Wait, a changeling! The same neurons, wired quite differently. Let us see how the Seer manages now.

speaker: clown
line: [relieved] And... he is himself again.

speaker: clown
line: [grand] By royal decree, his wiring is real. Everything else, we shall tell you plainly.

speaker: clown
line: [laughing] The very same neurons as our Prince. And yet its Seer could not find a princess in a room full of people.

speaker: clown
line: [playful] A fine effort, everyone. Mostly fine. Partly effort.

speaker: clown
line: [wry] The court will remember this trial. The court will try to forget it.
